scope: Completed course instruction, educator workshops and collaborative field sessions connect aerial mapping and field GIS with spatial analysis. Black Rock Forest balloon mapping precedes later drone work. Activities include classroom, indoor and outdoor work; participation does not by itself establish learning gains.

events.title: Black Rock Forest balloon aerial mapping and field GIS
events.place: Black Rock Forest, Cornwall, New York
events.program: Three Columbia GIS courses · Fall 2017
events.contributors: Kytt MacManus, Dara Mendeloff and Greg Yetman; teaching assistants Sara Lytle and Christina Paton; organizer Gina Dinnegan; participating GIS students
events.contribution: Three GIS courses worked with Public Lab balloon kits, visible-light and modified infrared camera observations, GPS and Collector for ArcGIS field mapping.
events.context: Balloon aerial mapping was an earlier field-instruction precursor. High winds limited the operation; the retained camera views are source photographs rather than validated maps or quantitative NDVI.

events.title: Structure-from-motion guest lecture
events.program: SDEV3450 · Spatial Analysis for Sustainable Development
events.contributors: Kytt MacManus, Jacqueline Ratner, Jonathan Sury
events.contribution: A guest lecture introduced structure-from-motion concepts and applications in spatial analysis.
events.context: Structure from motion reconstructs three-dimensional geometry from overlapping photographs. This session introduced the method in a classroom setting.

events.title: Tello drone laboratory
events.program: SDEV3450 · Spatial Analysis for Sustainable Development
events.contributors: Kytt MacManus, Juan Nathaniel

events.context: The laboratory focused on classroom practice and operational safety.

events.contribution: Students collected drone observations during a two-day field exercise, developed spatial analyses and contributed to a shared ArcGIS StoryMap.
events.context: The Provost award supported teaching equipment and software. Earth Institute support contributed to field travel.

events.contribution: An indoor equipment session introduced drone preparation and fieldwork arrangements for the Spatial Analysis course.

events.title: Staten Island course and community drone fieldwork

events.title: SDEV3450 winter field workshop

events.contributors: Kytt MacManus
events.contribution: A winter field workshop introduced drone-camera observations at Lamont, including visible-light imagery and thermal displays.
events.context: Thermal colors illustrate relative apparent surface-temperature patterns. Quantitative temperatures require the relevant calibration and acquisition information.

events.program: SDEV3450 · Spatial Analysis for Sustainable Development
events.contributors: Kytt MacManus

events.contribution: Building Climate Justice students attended a drone-operations workshop at Lamont, connecting field preparation with visible-light and thermal observations.

events.title: SDEV3450 field data collection at Hemlock Hill Farm
events.program: SDEV3450 · Watershed Agricultural Council collaboration
events.contributors: Kytt MacManus with Watershed Agricultural Council hosts
events.contribution: SDEV3450 students visited Hemlock Hill Farm for field-data collection with Watershed Agricultural Council hosts.
events.context: Ground control, positioning and total-station work were combined with photogrammetry, separately logged LiDAR acquisition and a multispectral camera configuration. Selected display derivatives document the field methods; agricultural outcomes and independent accuracy are not established.

events.title: SDEV4650 drone-data workshop at Lamont
events.program: SDEV4650 · Building Climate Justice
events.contributors: Kytt MacManus
events.contribution: A Lamont workshop connected drone data acquisition with survey and photogrammetric reconstruction products.
events.context: Photogrammetric products describe image-derived surface geometry. Their spatial resolution does not establish independent positional accuracy.
